notes: The Pi's GPIO header uses catalogue names: the diagram's GP15/GP25/GP8/GP7/GP21 are GPIO15/GPIO25/GPIO8/GPIO7/GPIO21; the ground pin next to GP3 (physical pin 6) is GND.1.
The long right-hand breadboard rail used as the ground rail is named 'tp.<n>' (rail row numbers are only approximate); it is treated as one continuous strip running the full length.
Pi-to-breadboard wires are male-to-female jumpers (female end 'a' on the Pi pin, male end 'b' in the breadboard). The single male-to-male jumper links the button's ground row to the ground rail.

LED legs and resistor legs are placed per the image: resistor from column e to column h in rows 9/15/21; LED anode in column j, cathode on the ground rail. The button's left legs are assumed in column e (wires in column d), right legs in column f straddling the centre gap.
Button: 1.l/1.r are one side, 2.l/2.r the other side; the button connects the ground wire row (28) to the GPIO21 row (30) when pressed.
The buzzer's + leg is assumed to be port 1 (in row 4, column j, fed by GPIO15), and its other leg goes to the ground rail. Amber LED is shown as a yellow LED.
Resistors are 330 ohm per the kit list; the manual's circuit image is the authority on placement.
